thread:
sre-team (customer): Hey team — after upgrading to @redwood/sdk v2.1.0 our Next.js SSR build started failing in production. Client side is fine, but server renders return 401s and the build log shows module resolution errors. Repro steps below. Anyone seen this?

jen (support): Sorry to hear that — can you paste the minimal error log and the package.json + bundler config? first pass: is this a bundler ESM/CJS thing or an auth header getting stripped?

sre-team (customer): Log:
```
Error: Request failed with status code 401
    at createError (/app/.heroku/node_modules/axios/lib/core/createError.js:16:15)
    at settle (/app/.heroku/node_modules/axios/lib/core/settle.js:17:12)
    at IncomingMessage.handleStreamEnd (/app/.heroku/node_modules/axios/lib/adapters/http.js:260:11)
Caused by: GET https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models -> 401 Unauthorized
```
Package.json (relevant):
```
{
  "dependencies": {
    "@redwood/sdk": "^2.1.0",
    "next": "13.4.6"
  },
  "type": "commonjs"
}
```
Next.js serverless build step fails earlier with: `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` referencing `dist/index.mjs` from the SDK when using our bundler config (turbo + esbuild). Locally `next dev` works though.

miguel (devex): Thanks — that sounds like two things colliding: conditional exports in the SDK's package.json and Next's SSR bundling for commonjs apps. Can you confirm whether you bundle node_modules or rely on server runtime to resolve? Also, does the 401 happen from the app or from a CDN/edge layer?

sre-team (customer): We bundle server code (esbuild) into a single artifact. The 401 appears only in prod after the bundle is deployed. Locally calling the API from a curl with the same env key returns 200, but inside the bundle it 401s.

elaine (eng): Repro hypothesis: when our exports map resolves to `./dist/index.mjs` for `import` paths, esbuild might rewrite imports and drop runtime header injection shim we use for SSR auth fallback. Two quick checks: 1) try pinning to v2.0.4 (previous) to see if behavior regresses back, 2) run a simple node script inside your build container that imports the SDK and does a request (to isolate bundling vs runtime).

sre-team (customer): Pinned to v2.0.4 — server bundle works and no 401s. So seems introduced in 2.1.0.

jen (support): Good repro. Can you share a tiny repro repo? If not possible, do a local bundle of a 1-file app: index.js that does `const r = require('@redwood/sdk')` and calls listModels; then run `npx esbuild --bundle index.js --platform=node --outfile=bundle.js` and run `node bundle.js`. If that returns 401 while unbundled returns 200, we can blame bundler resolution.

sre-team (customer): Did that. Bundled -> 401, unbundled -> 200. I can attach the bundle output if useful.

miguel (devex): Please paste the top of the SDK's resolved file path inside the bundle (search for `@redwood/sdk`). Also include your esbuild flags.

sre-team (customer): Esbuild flags: `--platform=node --bundle --target=node18`. In bundle I see: `require("./node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/index.mjs")` (odd for require to point to .mjs).

elaine (eng): That's the smoking gun. When bundlers resolve a .mjs entry behind a CommonJS wrapper, runtime interop sometimes causes our auth middleware to be elided. We recently changed package exports to prefer `./dist/index.mjs` for import paths which broke certain bundlers when the consumer package.json.type = "commonjs". We'll patch.

deploy-bot: new release candidate created: @redwood/sdk@2.1.1-rc.1 — tests: packaging (exports map), node E2E on node14/16/18.

jen (support): Short-term workaround for customers: 1) pin to @redwood/sdk@2.0.4 OR 2) add an explicit require alias in your bundler to resolve `@redwood/sdk` -> `@redwood/sdk/dist/index.cjs` (CJS entry) OR 3) set `type: "module"` and switch to native ESM if feasible. We should doc these in a support KB.

sre-team (customer): Workaround 2 worked for us (forced resolution to cjs entry). Can you confirm if v2.1.1-rc.1 will be safe to unpin? We'd like to upgrade.

elaine (eng): RC includes a fix: add a dual-entry exports map that exposes explicit `./cjs` entry and ensures `require()` resolves to `.cjs`. We also added a small shim so that auth header injection is preserved when bundlers rewrite import extensions. Please try 2.1.1-rc.1 in a staging deploy and report back.

sre-team (customer): Installing rc now. Quick note: we saw a spike of retry loops after the upgrade (our telemetry showed bursts of 429 then 401). Could this be the same root cause?

miguel (devex): Yes likely: if auth header missing, SDK retries can trigger 429s from downstream quota protections and then 401s. Check your app logs for `SDK_AUTHTOKEN` header presence in outgoing requests.

sre-team (customer): Confirmed — bundle outbound HTTP calls don't include `authorization` header when using 2.1.0. After switching to 2.1.1-rc.1 headers are back.

jen (support): Great. Action items: 
- eng: push 2.1.1 with the exports map fix and tests for commonjs bundling (elaine)
- devex: add KB + upgrade guidance + esbuild alias snippet (miguel)
- support: notify customers who reported similar 401s with the workaround/pin (jen)

elaine (eng): I'll push 2.1.1 tomorrow and include a small automated test that bundles with esbuild in commonjs mode and asserts outgoing request headers preserved.

miguel (devex): KB snippet for esbuild alias: add to build config: 
```js
// esbuild plugin example
resolve: {
  alias: {
    '@redwood/sdk': require.resolve('@redwood/sdk/dist/index.cjs')
  }
}
```
Also mention Next.js users should prefer not bundling node_modules server-side or set `externals` for the SDK.

sre-team (customer): Thanks everyone — staging with 2.1.1-rc.1 looks good so far. Will promote to prod after smoke tests. :+1:

jen (support): Marking this thread for follow-up; will send a postmortem blurb once 2.1.1 is out. Thanks for quick repro and testing. :rocket:

deploy-bot: release @redwood/sdk@2.1.1 published (sha: abcd1234) — changelog: fix(exports): cjs/esm conditional exports to avoid bundler auth shim being elided.

sre-team (customer): Upgraded to 2.1.1 in prod — no more 401s. Logging looks clean. Appreciate the fast turnaround.
